sections.title: Establish that the work is comparable
paragraphs:
[ReceptionHQ's pricing](https://www.receptionhq.com/pricing/) presents call-based and minute-based service families. Their tasks are not automatically identical. Before using a formula, confirm that both quotes include your required intake, transfer or scheduling outcome and the same coverage period.

Revo's [current plans](/pricing) publish included minutes. This guide does not create a Revo per-call plan or invent its additional-usage rate. Use the rate and rules in your actual offer.

sections.title: Copy this ledger and apply both contracts
paragraphs:
The following calls and prices are deliberately hypothetical, not provider quotes. Every call counts under both example offers. The minute offer rounds each individual call up to a whole minute.

| Same call | Actual duration | Call-based units | Minute-based units |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: ordinary inquiry | 1 minute 10 seconds | 1 | 2 |
| B: longer intake | 4 minutes 5 seconds | 1 | 5 |
| C: repeat caller | 35 seconds | 1 | 1 |
| D: short message | 20 seconds | 1 | 1 |
| Total | 6 minutes 10 seconds | 4 calls | 9 billed minutes |

Example call offer: $20 base, two included calls, $3 per additional call. Its total for this ledger is $20 + (4 − 2) × $3 = $26.

Example minute offer: $20 base, five included minutes, $2 per additional minute. Its total for the identical ledger is $20 + (9 − 5) × $2 = $28.

This example establishes arithmetic only. Different real rates, longer calls or different rounding can reverse the result. Do not extrapolate four fictional calls into an expected saving.

sections.title: Replace every example rule with the written offer
paragraphs:
For each quote, compute base + max(0, billable units − included units) × additional-unit rate, then add applicable required charges. If the offer has tiers or other pricing logic, use that logic instead.

Record whether spam, repeated callers, unanswered transfers, hold time, outbound follow-up and test calls are billed. Check whether rounding occurs per call or across the whole period. A provider that counts unique customers requires a third model, not relabeling its allowance as calls.

Use one representative real period, remove unnecessary personal information, and retain both original durations and contract-adjusted units. Ask the supplier to confirm your calculation. Keep service quality and task eligibility as separate decision columns; a cheaper calculation cannot prove the required outcome works.

Published by Revo, a competing provider. This is a documentary procurement guide reviewed October 29, 2026, not a configuration tutorial or hands-on product test.

## Identify the components in the actual proposal

The official [3CX receptionist page](https://www.3cx.com/phone-system/ai-receptionist/) describes AI greeting, information capture and routing within its phone system. Its [agent configuration documentation](https://www.3cx.com/docs/ai-agent-configuration/) establishes an external AI-provider connection and the applicable AI Edition requirements. Confirm supported OpenAI or xAI configuration against the current edition and release.

3CX prices its system by annual licensing and simultaneous-call capacity rather than treating every employee as an independent reception subscription. That license is not the complete cost of AI usage or telephony. Obtain the exact applicable edition and capacity from [3CX pricing](https://www.3cx.com/ordering/pricing/).

## Allocate each bill and operating responsibility

| Component | Evidence and owner to establish |
| --- | --- |
| 3CX license | Edition, renewal and required simultaneous-call capacity |
| AI provider | Supported account, model, usage charges and budget owner |
| Number and carrier | Existing arrangement, required routes and separate charges |
| Hosting and administration | Who maintains the deployment, updates and account access? |
| Reception instructions | Who approves service information and exception behavior? |
| Acceptance and later changes | Who tests a route change and restores the agreed fallback? |

A licensing count is not a promise of unlimited concurrent AI calls. Ask how capacity is allocated when reception, transfers and ordinary office calls occur together. Keep any sensitive credentials out of a sales worksheet.

## Use a contractor-specific decision test

A fictional roofing office already has 3CX extensions for its estimator and coordinator. It wants routine inquiries collected when both are busy. Request a demonstration from an incoming call through the approved intake to the intended employee or fallback record. Do not assume meeting scheduling means a confirmed field visit, or that a native phone agent can inspect a repair, authorize a price or update an unsupported job system. Have the administrator identify which required actions the actual deployment can perform.

## When a managed reception offer is a better comparison

If nobody in your business or contracted IT team will own the PBX and model configuration, compare a managed answering arrangement on its own scope. [Revo](/pricing) publishes AI reception, supported booking and summaries with plan-specific transfers. This guide establishes no 3CX integration, external model administration or complete PBX replacement for Revo.

The separate [build-versus-buy guide](/ai-answering-service/compare/build-vs-buy-ai-receptionist) considers architecture generally. This page identifies the specific 3CX license and operating responsibilities your proposal must cover.

### Does paying for 3CX establish that AI usage is included?

No. Confirm the edition, external provider usage, telephony and any administration costs separately.

### Should every small contractor buy a PBX-native agent?

No. It depends on the existing system, required outcome and who will operate it.

[Compare Revo's current plans](/pricing) with the complete 3CX proposal rather than a license price alone.
